invariants_created: Host header is mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request; must appear in request headers
Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header is required when a request or response includes a body
POST, PUT, and PATCH requests should include a body with a Content-Type header
HEAD response must not include a message body
3xx redirect responses must include a Location header specifying the redirect target URI
After receiving 401 Unauthorized, the client must retry the request with an Authorization header containing valid credentials
After receiving 301 Moved Permanently or 302 Found, the client should follow the Location header and reissue the request to the new URI
Connection: keep-alive allows multiple request-response cycles on a single TCP connection; Connection: close signals the connection will be terminated after the response
Request line must precede all headers; headers must precede the empty line (CRLF CRLF); body (if any) follows the empty line
OPTIONS * targets the server as a whole rather than a specific resource path

INIT state transitions to CONNECTED after TCP connection establishment; CONNECTED transitions to RESPONSE_PENDING after sending a request; RESPONSE_PENDING transitions to IDLE on successful 2xx response; IDLE allows new requests on keep-alive connections
CONNECTED state transitions to CLOSED when Connection: close is received or sent with the response
HTTP_REQUEST.Host: Mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request; must not be omitted
HTTP_REQUEST.Content-Length: Required when request body is present; must accurately reflect body byte length; mutually exclusive with Transfer-Encoding for framing
HTTP_REQUEST.Transfer-Encoding: Alternative to Content-Length for body framing; 'chunked' value enables streaming; mutually exclusive with Content-Length for message framing
HTTP_REQUEST.Content-Type: Should be present when request includes a body (POST, PUT, PATCH); indicates MIME type of body payload
HTTP_REQUEST.Authorization: Must be included when retrying after a 401 Unauthorized response; format depends on WWW-Authenticate challenge scheme
HTTP_REQUEST.Connection: Controls connection persistence: 'keep-alive' (default in HTTP/1.1) allows reuse; 'close' terminates after response
HTTP_REQUEST.Method: Must be one of: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, CONNECT, TRACE; determines safe/idempotent semantics
HTTP_REQUEST.Request-URI: Typically an absolute path (e.g., /resource); '*' for server-level OPTIONS; must be a valid URI
HTTP_RESPONSE.Status-Code: 3-digit integer: 2xx=success, 3xx=redirection, 4xx=client error, 5xx=server error; determines client state transition
HTTP_RESPONSE.Location: Must be present in 3xx redirect responses (301, 302); contains the target URI for redirection
HTTP_RESPONSE.Content-Length: Required when response body is present; must not be present for HEAD responses, 204 No Content, or 304 Not Modified
HTTP_RESPONSE.Set-Cookie: Server-side session management; client must store and echo back via Cookie header in subsequent requests
HTTP_RESPONSE.WWW-Authenticate: Must accompany 401 Unauthorized responses; specifies authentication scheme and realm
HTTP_RESPONSE.Connection: If 'close', client must not reuse the TCP connection; if 'keep-alive' or absent (default), connection may be reused

examples: Content negotiation; acceptable response MIME types
Credentials for protected resources (sent after 401 challenge)
Byte length of request body; required when body present
MIME type of request body (required for POST/PUT/PATCH with body)
Target resource path (e.g., /path, or * for OPTIONS server-level)
Alternative to Content-Length; 'chunked' for streaming bodies
Redirect target URI; present in 3xx responses
Human-readable status description (e.g., OK, Not Found)
Server sets session/state cookie on client
3-digit integer classifying response (2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error)
